newsitem.title: PERU: Peace talks in Peru crisis to resume Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Peace talks in Peru crisis to resume Wednesday.

text.p: Talks between the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima will resume later on Wednesday, a member of the talks guarantors' commission said.
"This afternoon talks start again," Archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani told reporters.

Cipriani made the brief statement after he and two other guarantors -- Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent and Michel Minnig of the Red Cross -- met rebel leader Nestor Cerpa inside the besieged Japanese residence for an hour and 20 minutes.
Cipriani and Vincent met government negotiator Domingo Palermo on Tuesday as part of efforts to peruade the sides back to the negotiating table for the first time in a week.

Talks to end the siege peacefully seemed to be progressing until the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), whose guerrillas are holding the hostages, broke off negotiations last Thursday and charged the government with planning to take the building by storm via a secret tunnel.
After meetings with both sides, the guarantors arranged a fresh round of talks, only to have the government call off the meeting, accusing the rebels of trying to backtrack on progress already made.
